findings.quote: and it would have gone on shortening it without any limit however large the fleet was allowed to grow
findings.note: B is an unbounded absolute and D shifts the axis to fault type rather than to fleet size, so two options fall on form. A vs C (both region types vs only the diversifying ones) is a real contrast the passage must settle.

findings.quote: Because a network can never lose only a little connectivity to a fault unless every single one of its routes is fully duplicated by a second cable laid alongside.
findings.note: B is a blanket 'can never ... unless every single' absolute and C is a generic repair-process fact that does not explain the contrast the stem poses; both fall on form. A remains a substantive confound (calmer waters), so A vs D still needs the passage.

findings.quote: That the Wenmarch Assurance Office had ordered all of its own correspondence to be kept and filed on the folding size.
findings.note: ARGUABLE: the option is verbatim true — "ordered its entire correspondence to be kept on the folding size and had its filing cabinets built to fit" — and it names the paragraph's headline event, so an examinee reading for "what made the folding size spread" can land on it. The case only survives by ignoring both delimiters in the prompt ("among ordinary firms", "once the Assurance Office had adopted it"): the text's actual transmission mechanism is the option A clause — "the cabinet makers, rather than tool up twice, began offering only the one size; and a firm that bought those cabinets found the folding sheet was the sheet that fitted the drawer". Key support is clearly stronger than the distractor case.

findings.quote: That a sheet proportion elegant enough to survive folding was always bound to be recognised as the best one and duly written into the rules.
findings.note: 'always bound to be' — teleological absolute, form-only elimination; it is also the position q:5's stem attributes to Ferrowby, i.e. the named foil.

findings.quote: That every size in the paper family is simply the size above it folded in half, which is what makes the folding proportion so convenient to use.
findings.note: True-but-definitional: no thesis, so it cannot be the main idea of a history item. Two eliminations leave C vs D, and q:3/q:4 stems (both presupposing the 1913 order drove uptake) push C without the passage.

findings.quote: It rose steadily until, within a few years, every paper-using firm in the whole trade had gone over entirely to the folding size.
findings.note: 'every ... in the whole trade ... entirely' — universal overreach, discardable on form.

findings.quote: It spread only after the government stepped in and made the folding size compulsory for all official and commercial correspondence.
findings.note: Retired cross-question rather than by form: q:4's stem asserts the Assurance Office's adoption is what spread the size among ordinary firms, which excludes a government mandate and also excludes A ('changed little'), leaving the concrete-figures option D decidable without reading the passage.

findings.quote: That the new filing cabinets were physically incapable of holding any sheet but the folding size, leaving every firm that bought one no other option at all.
findings.note: Absolute twin of A ('physically incapable', 'no other option at all'): same mechanism at implausible strength, so the hedged member of the pair is the form-favoured pick.

findings.quote: That the office publicised the folding proportion's geometric advantages until other firms were persuaded of its merits and chose to switch across.
findings.note: The stem's 'actually spread' signals a non-obvious mechanism and so disfavours persuasion-by-merit. B remains substantive (an office filing rule can pull correspondents along), so the item is not decided — better than chance, not a giveaway.

findings.quote: In full agreement: she too concludes that a proportion that good needed no lucky customer and would sooner or later have prevailed anywhere on its own.
findings.note: Absolute version of A ('needed no lucky customer', 'anywhere on its own') — eliminable by form.

findings.quote: Openly scornful: she regards the folding sheet as a poor choice that a single office ended up forcing on an unwilling and resistant trade.
findings.note: Off-target extreme: the quoted claim is about inevitability, not about the sheet's quality. A and B both survive as substantive authorial stances within the question; only q:1's contrastive main-idea option decides B.
